authority: User accepted the proposal to distinguish success payloads from failures with an internal status tag.

confirmed.rule: Every CS execution produces an INTERNAL tagged outcome with a status of OK or ERROR. The tag is authoritative for success/failure; never infer status from the human-readable return value.

On internal status OK, payload presence is represented independently from the payload's content. No payload means public CSo emits plain OK; an existing payload means public CSo emits that exact command response without a success envelope.

An OK result whose payload is the literal string ERROR remains SUCCESS, not an ERROR. A returned literal OK is likewise a valid successful payload; even None/False/0/empty string must not be mistaken for missing payload.

On internal status ERROR, the outcome carries one Error record/reference from the shared Error System Lib. Public CSo reports failure according to that unified ERROR semantic contract, independently of text.
Error Buffer and mandatory failure-linked CS logging depend on the INTERNAL status ERROR and real execution context, never on string matching the CSo display payload.
BOOT and non-CS component Errors still use Error System Lib; this does not require fabricating a CS result or command.

canonical_minimum.value: original command result, present iff OK and payload_present=true
canonical_minimum.error: shared Error record/reference, present iff ERROR

boundaries.transport_text_only: A text-only projection of success data ERROR is visually ambiguous with error text; any machine-readable CSo interface must preserve the internal status on a separate channel or typed representation. Exact transport mapping remains OPEN.
boundaries.unrelated_open: Exact Error-record fields, Error.report API, invocation correlation and logging sink/FILE details stay OPEN.
boundaries.no_new_hardcore: Result typing remains internal to HC.CS; Error is still shared System Lib.
